rationale: After a generic, US-flavoured opener (garbage disposal, breaker), the assistant adapted well to UK wiring, covered the fused spur, door-top controls on an integrated Neff, and a possible plug under the sink, and escalated sensibly to Neff service/independent engineer with a useful summary to quote. Safety was sound throughout (fuse swaps only with power off, no live testing). Weaknesses: it largely dismissed the spur fuse on the basis of a lit neon ('usually fine') rather than suggesting borrowing a kettle's 13A fuse to try in the spur, which the ground truth lists as a sensible direction; it named likely internal parts (power module, mains filter) somewhat speculatively though without recommending purchase; and the reset/plug-check steps were repeated across messages. The model number was only requested at the very end.
